clue.text: Concerned with the landlord being antimonarchist

parts.note: re means concerning or with regard to
a publican is the landlord who runs a pub

explanation.surface: A pub landlord is revealed to want the monarchy abolished.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who opposes kings and queens favours a state with an elected head instead.

clue.text: Stray animal with nothing inside it

indicators.note: inside it tells us the nothing goes within the animal just named

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep, an animal
nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A wandering beast is found to have an empty belly.
explanation.definitionFit: To stray is to wander about aimlessly.

clue.text: Trial period for cricketer no-one backed

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
a bat is a batsman in cricket

indicators.note: backed means the letters for no and one are read from the end

parts.note: no is NO and one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A cricketer nobody supports is given a trial period in the team.
explanation.definitionFit: Probation is a spell of testing a newcomer or offender before full acceptance.

clue.text: Do vote with the opposition!

explanation.surface: A rallying call to vote against the government.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: to vote with the opposition is to 'be a no'. A beano is British slang for a lively party.
explanation.definitionFit: A do is a party, as is a beano; voting with the opposition makes you a no voter.

clue.text: Isn't worried over work er for the moment

indicators.note: in a down answer the first part sits over the second
worried means the letters of isn't are disturbed and rearranged

parts.note: the printed 'work er' is the word worker split by the page; a worker is an ant

explanation.surface: Someone is unconcerned about a worker for now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges the letters of isn't; the page splits worker as 'work er', and 'over' places the shuffle above the ant in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: An instant is a very brief moment of time.

clue.text: A hold-up a conservationist body finds hard

parts.note: a dam holds up a river's water
NT is the National Trust, a British heritage conservation charity

explanation.surface: A conservation charity finds a delay difficult to deal with.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is a British body that preserves historic houses and landscapes.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant originally meant an unbreakable stone, so firm and unyielding.

clue.text: Beginning well, a member will be genial

indicators.note: beginning means only the opening letter of well is taken

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A new member who starts well will prove friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: A warm person is friendly and cordial.

clue.text: A man who is representative

parts.note: gent is short for gentleman, a man

explanation.surface: Asking which man is the representative.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent acts on behalf of someone else.

clue.text: Beds for fellows wanting hair stuffing

indicators.note: stuffing means the hair is packed inside the fellows

parts.note: mates are companions, fellows
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Beds for men in need of horsehair filling.
explanation.definitionFit: Mattresses are the padded parts of beds, so beds by metonymy.

clue.text: Warning the girl in question to take key

indicators.note: to take means the rearranged letters receive the key inside them
in question means the letters of the girl are doubtful and rearranged

parts.note: D is a musical key

explanation.surface: A warning to the girl concerned to pick up her key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the girl in question' looks like a person, but 'in question' signals a rearrangement, and 'to take' has that rearrangement swallow the musical key.
explanation.definitionFit: A red light is a signal to stop, a danger warning.

clue.text: A strange ring given at farewell in Hawaii

indicators.note: strange means the letters of the ring word are odd and rearranged

parts.note: a halo is a ring of light

explanation.surface: A strange circlet is presented at a Hawaiian goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloha is the Hawaiian greeting used for both hello and goodbye.

clue.text: Declaration of country people having time

parts.note: a state is a country
men are people

explanation.surface: A national announcement by people with time on their hands.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement is a formal declaration or announcement.

clue.text: Prospect for gold in Central America

parts.note: Panama is a country in Central America
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Panning for gold in Central America.
explanation.definitionFit: A panorama is a broad view, a prospect over the landscape.

clue.text: After a little doggy pal a terrier maybe

indicators.note: a little means only a small run of letters is taken from the words that follow

explanation.surface: Following a small dog's pal, perhaps a terrier.
explanation.definitionFit: Later means after in time, subsequently.

clue.text: Keeps old husband totally idle

parts.note: a shop that keeps goods stocks them
to husband land in an old sense is to farm or till it

explanation.surface: A frugal old husband keeps a thoroughly lazy life.
explanation.definitionFit: Stock-still means completely motionless, doing nothing at all.

clue.text: A child of three

parts.note: looks like a three-year-old, but means one of three children born together

explanation.definitionFit: A triplet is one of three offspring born at a single birth.

clue.text: Belgian subjects?

parts.note: feudal vassals read whimsically as citizens of the Belgian city Liège

explanation.definitionFit: Liegemen were vassals bound to serve a lord; split up, the word suggests men of a Belgian city.

clue.text: Gets tea out. That could be a bloomer

indicators.note: out means the letters of gets tea are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone serves tea, which could prove a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a mistake, but it means a flowering plant: the genus of marigolds.
explanation.definitionFit: Tagetes is the marigold genus, plants that flower.

clue.text: Weight accorded to a crossing-place in town

parts.note: a ton is a unit of weight
a bridge is a place to cross a river

explanation.surface: A heavy load is granted access to a town crossing.
explanation.walkthrough: Tonbridge is a market town in Kent, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonbridge is a Kentish town on the River Medway.

clue.text: Well-satisfied constituent

explanation.definitionFit: Content means pleased or satisfied; stressed differently, the content of something is what it is made up of.

clue.text: Beam, having dashed in most elevated

indicators.note: in means the word for dashed goes within the other part
elevated in a down clue means the word most is turned upward, read bottom to top

parts.note: dashed means ran

explanation.surface: A beam rushed into the highest point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most elevated' looks like a superlative meaning highest, but 'elevated' turns the word most upward in this down light, and 'in' puts the running word inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A transom is a horizontal crossbar or beam over a door or window.

clue.text: Show a scholar money a couple of notes

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is a scholar
tin is British slang for money
E is a musical note, taken twice

explanation.surface: A show for which a scholar pays money and a couple of banknotes.
explanation.definitionFit: A matinee is an afternoon performance of a show.

clue.text: He painted pictures of sea-mist, all obscure

indicators.note: all obscure means the letters of sea-mist are confused and rearranged

explanation.surface: An artist painted scenes of fog at sea, everything blurred.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was a French artist famous for colourful canvases.

clue.text: Gain an impression of sound reasoning

explanation.definitionFit: To sense is to perceive; good sense is sound judgement.

clue.text: Steals — prison's indicated!

explanation.walkthrough: Nick is British slang both for to steal and for a prison or police station; 'prison's' is read as 'the nick is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To nick is to pinch something; a nick is a jail.

clue.text: Create a stir, try imaginative workmanship

indicators.note: create means the letters of a stir and try are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Making a fuss and trying out inventive craft.
explanation.definitionFit: Artistry is creative skill and craftsmanship.

clue.text: Go astray going over good part of the Middle East

indicators.note: in a down answer one part goes over the other

parts.note: to sin is to go astray morally
AI, read as A1, means first-rate or good

explanation.surface: Wandering off course across a region of the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinai is the peninsula of Egypt linking Africa to Asia.

clue.text: Fortitude is called for on icy roads

definitions.text: is called for on icy roads

explanation.definitionFit: Grit means courage and stamina; it is also the sand and gravel spread on frozen streets.

clue.text: Expands popular lines

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
creases are lines or folds

explanation.surface: Popular wrinkles spreading.
explanation.definitionFit: Increases means grows or enlarges.

clue.text: Deep depression caused by drain trouble

indicators.note: trouble means the letters of drain are stirred up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A low mood caused by a blocked drain.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point, a figurative deep low.

clue.text: Register British currency first

parts.note: L stands for the pound sterling

explanation.surface: Putting British money first on the register.
explanation.definitionFit: A list is a register or roll of names.
